title: Profile pack config draft (runtime tuning profiles) — format + H100/L40S examples
content:
Context
- This is an EARLY DRAFT of the “hardware tuning profiles pack” config format.
- Goal: a single artifact that the runtime can load to select safe + performant defaults per GPU SKU + environment characteristics.
- This draft focuses on H100 + L40S. B200 intentionally omitted here (will need a compatibility gate / explicit opt-in).

Design principles (draft)
1) Deterministic selection: for a given (sku, form_factor, vram, driver, cuda, mig, model_family, workload_bucket) we pick exactly one profile.
2) Safety-first defaults: profiles must specify guardrails (memory headroom, concurrency caps, queue limits). Avoid footguns.
3) Overrideability with auditability: allow overrides (Dedicated/Private) but require “explainable diffs” and enforce constraints.
4) Versioned pack: runtime logs active profile_id + pack_version; canary + rollback can operate at pack_version granularity.

Non-goals for v1
- Encoding every model-specific knob as first-class schema fields (we’ll start with a small stable set).
- Automatic “learning” of settings; we are packaging known-good settings + selection logic.


Proposed file format
- Human-authored source: YAML (committed in redwood runtime repo) w/ comments.
- Runtime distribution: JSON (compiled/validated) embedded in the runtime image OR fetched by control plane.
- This doc uses YAML-like examples with comments; the compiled JSON would be equivalent.

Top-level schema (draft)

pack_version: string
# Semver-ish: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
# - MAJOR: schema changes / incompatible selection behavior changes
# - MINOR: new profiles or tuned defaults
# - PATCH: bugfixes, guardrail tightening, comment-only does NOT bump

schema_version: string
# Used for validation in runtime. Example: "1"

metadata:
  owner_team: string                  # e.g., "eng-serving-runtime"
  release_train: string               # e.g., "runtime-1.22"
  created_at: YYYY-MM-DD
  last_modified: YYYY-MM-DD

selection:
  # Defines precedence and tie-break rules when multiple profiles match.
  precedence:
    - "explicit_customer_pin"         # Dedicated/Private provided profile_id or profile_version pin
    - "fleet_default"                 # Hosted defaults, or Dedicated default if not pinned
    - "pack_fallback"                 # last resort (must always exist for supported SKUs)

  tie_break:
    - "highest_priority"              # integer within a profile
    - "most_specific_match"           # more constrained selector wins
    - "newest_profile_revision"       # profile metadata revision counter

  compatibility_mode:
    # How strictly to enforce driver/CUDA constraints.
    # strict: refuse to start if no compatible profile
    # permissive: start with pack_fallback + log error + degrade features
    hosted: "strict"
    dedicated: "strict"
    private: "permissive"             # NOTE: maybe strict too? open question below.


profiles: list
# Each entry describes selectors + knob values.

profile schema (draft)

- profile_id: string
  priority: integer
  status: "active" | "deprecated" | "blocked"
  description: string

  selectors:
    # Each selector field is optional. Omitted means “match all”.
    # If multiple profiles match, tie_break resolves.

    gpu:
      sku: "H100" | "L40S" | "B200" | ...
      form_factor: "SXM" | "PCIE" | "UNKNOWN"   # if we can’t detect reliably
      vram_gb: 80 | 94 | 48 | 0                     # 0 means unknown
      mig:
        mode: "disabled" | "enabled" | "any"
        profile: string                              # e.g., "1g.10gb"; optional

    software:
      driver:
        min: string                                  # e.g., "550.54"
        max_exclusive: string                         # e.g., "560.00" (optional)
      cuda:
        min: string                                   # e.g., "12.2"
        max_exclusive: string                          # optional

    deployment:
      mode: "hosted" | "dedicated" | "private" | "any"
      region: string                                  # optional; usually not needed

    model:
      family: "llama" | "mistral" | "qwen" | "embedding" | "any"
      quantization: "fp16" | "bf16" | "int8" | "fp8" | "any"
      max_context_tokens_lte: integer                  # used to select long-context behavior

    workload:
      bucket: "chat_short" | "chat_mixed" | "chat_long" | "embeddings" | "rerank" | "any"

  guardrails:
    # Hard safety constraints. Validation should fail if violated by knobs.
    min_free_vram_gb: number                          # e.g., 6.0
    max_gpu_util_p99_target: number                   # hint/target; not a hard constraint
    max_concurrent_requests: integer                  # hard cap
    max_inflight_tokens: integer                      # cap across prefill+decode
    max_queue_depth: integer                          # scheduler admission control

  knobs:
    # Runtime tuning knobs. Prefer stable names, avoid “raw env var soup” when possible.

    kernel:
      attention:
        implementation: "flash" | "flash_v3" | "triton" | "auto"
        allow_fallback: true|false
        fallback_order: "flash_v3,flash,triton"      # comma-separated
      matmul:
        fp8_enabled: true|false
        bf16_accumulation: true|false

    scheduler:
      mode: "continuous_batching" | "static" | "auto"
      max_batch_tokens: integer
      max_batch_size: integer
      prefill_decode_policy: "balanced" | "prefill_priority" | "decode_priority"
      queueing:
        max_queue_ms: integer                          # soft limit; prefer admission control over waiting
        enable_backpressure: true|false

    kv_cache:
      page_size_kb: integer                            # allocator granularity
      reserved_vram_fraction: number                   # e.g., 0.18
      compaction:
        enabled: true|false
        trigger_fragmentation_pct: number              # e.g., 12.0
        max_compaction_ms_per_minute: integer          # avoid compaction storms

    memory:
      allocator: "cuda_malloc_async" | "jemalloc" | "default"
      enable_hugepages: true|false                     # host-level best-effort; see host section
      fragmentation_oom_guard: true|false              # if true: reduce concurrency when fragmentation signal high

    host_recommendations:
      # These are NOT always enforceable; runtime can log warnings + export a “host_ok” boolean.
      required:
        - "nvidia_driver_min"
      best_effort:
        - "cpu_pinning"
        - "numa_alignment"
        - "hugepages"
      notes: string

    observability:
      emit_profile_tags: true|false
      log_startup_summary: true|false
      kernel_choice_metric: true|false
      scheduler_queue_ms_metric: true|false


Example config (H100 + L40S)

pack_version: "1.0.0-draft.3"
schema_version: "1"
metadata:
  owner_team: "eng-serving-runtime"
  release_train: "runtime-1.22"
  created_at: "2026-01-16"
  last_modified: "2026-02-08"

selection:
  precedence:
    - "explicit_customer_pin"
    - "fleet_default"
    - "pack_fallback"
  tie_break:
    - "highest_priority"
    - "most_specific_match"
    - "newest_profile_revision"
  compatibility_mode:
    hosted: "strict"
    dedicated: "strict"
    private: "permissive"

profiles:
  # -------------------------
  # H100 (SXM, 80GB)
  # -------------------------

  - profile_id: "h100-sxm80-chat_mixed-v1"
    priority: 100
    status: "active"
    description: "H100 SXM 80GB tuned for mixed prompt lengths; aims to protect tail latency while keeping throughput high."

    selectors:
      gpu:
        sku: "H100"
        form_factor: "SXM"
        vram_gb: 80
        mig:
          mode: "disabled"
      software:
        driver:
          min: "550.54"
        cuda:
          min: "12.2"
      deployment:
        mode: "any"
      model:
        family: "any"
        quantization: "bf16"
        max_context_tokens_lte: 32768
      workload:
        bucket: "chat_mixed"

    guardrails:
      min_free_vram_gb: "8.0"                 # string in compiled JSON? (implementation detail)
      max_gpu_util_p99_target: "0.92"
      max_concurrent_requests: "96"
      max_inflight_tokens: "110000"
      max_queue_depth: "160"

    knobs:
      kernel:
        attention:
          implementation: "flash_v3"          # from kernel team microbench results (Jan 2026)
          allow_fallback: "true"
          fallback_order: "flash_v3,flash,triton"
        matmul:
          fp8_enabled: "true"                 # NOTE: safe w/ bf16 weights? depends on model; gate by model family?
          bf16_accumulation: "true"

      scheduler:
        mode: "continuous_batching"
        max_batch_tokens: "8192"
        max_batch_size: "64"
        prefill_decode_policy: "balanced"
        queueing:
          max_queue_ms: "20"
          enable_backpressure: "true"

      kv_cache:
        page_size_kb: "64"
        reserved_vram_fraction: "0.16"
        compaction:
          enabled: "true"
          trigger_fragmentation_pct: "10.0"
          max_compaction_ms_per_minute: "400"

      memory:
        allocator: "cuda_malloc_async"
        enable_hugepages: "false"             # runtime can’t enforce; move to host_recommendations
        fragmentation_oom_guard: "true"

      host_recommendations:
        required:
          - "nvidia_driver_min"
        best_effort:
          - "cpu_pinning"
          - "numa_alignment"
          - "hugepages"
        notes: "SXM nodes: prefer CPU pinning to NIC + GPU locality; enable hugepages only if host is stable."

      observability:
        emit_profile_tags: "true"
        log_startup_summary: "true"
        kernel_choice_metric: "true"
        scheduler_queue_ms_metric: "true"


  # H100 fallback (any form factor, any workload)
  - profile_id: "h100-fallback-safe-v1"
    priority: 10
    status: "active"
    description: "Conservative fallback for H100. Lower concurrency, larger KV headroom."

    selectors:
      gpu:
        sku: "H100"
      software:
        driver:
          min: "550.54"
      workload:
        bucket: "any"

    guardrails:
      min_free_vram_gb: "10.0"
      max_gpu_util_p99_target: "0.88"
      max_concurrent_requests: "64"
      max_inflight_tokens: "80000"
      max_queue_depth: "120"

    knobs:
      kernel:
        attention:
          implementation: "auto"
          allow_fallback: "true"
          fallback_order: "flash,flash_v3,triton"
        matmul:
          fp8_enabled: "false"                # conservative until per-model gating exists
          bf16_accumulation: "true"

      scheduler:
        mode: "continuous_batching"
        max_batch_tokens: "6144"
        max_batch_size: "48"
        prefill_decode_policy: "prefill_priority"  # protect interactive latency
        queueing:
          max_queue_ms: "15"
          enable_backpressure: "true"

      kv_cache:
        page_size_kb: "64"
        reserved_vram_fraction: "0.18"
        compaction:
          enabled: "true"
          trigger_fragmentation_pct: "8.0"
          max_compaction_ms_per_minute: "300"

      memory:
        allocator: "cuda_malloc_async"
        fragmentation_oom_guard: "true"

      host_recommendations:
        required:
          - "nvidia_driver_min"
        best_effort:
          - "cpu_pinning"
          - "numa_alignment"
        notes: "Use this if any p99 regression is observed; easiest rollback target."

      observability:
        emit_profile_tags: "true"
        log_startup_summary: "true"
        kernel_choice_metric: "true"
        scheduler_queue_ms_metric: "true"


  # -------------------------
  # L40S (48GB) — tighter memory, more conservative concurrency
  # -------------------------

  - profile_id: "l40s-pcie48-chat_mixed-v1"
    priority: 100
    status: "active"
    description: "L40S 48GB tuned to avoid OOM/fragmentation under burst traffic; lower concurrency, higher KV headroom."

    selectors:
      gpu:
        sku: "L40S"
        form_factor: "PCIE"
        vram_gb: 48
        mig:
          mode: "any"                      # NOTE: L40S MIG policy unclear; probably disable? open question.
      software:
        driver:
          min: "550.54"
        cuda:
          min: "12.2"
      deployment:
        mode: "any"
      model:
        family: "any"
        quantization: "bf16"
        max_context_tokens_lte: 16384
      workload:
        bucket: "chat_mixed"

    guardrails:
      min_free_vram_gb: "7.0"              # higher relative headroom than H100 due to fragmentation sensitivity
      max_gpu_util_p99_target: "0.85"
      max_concurrent_requests: "28"
      max_inflight_tokens: "32000"
      max_queue_depth: "60"

    knobs:
      kernel:
        attention:
          implementation: "flash"          # L40S: prefer stable kernel; flash_v3 may not be consistently better
          allow_fallback: "true"
          fallback_order: "flash,triton"
        matmul:
          fp8_enabled: "false"
          bf16_accumulation: "true"

      scheduler:
        mode: "continuous_batching"
        max_batch_tokens: "4096"
        max_batch_size: "24"
        prefill_decode_policy: "prefill_priority"   # protect interactive traffic; throughput is secondary
        queueing:
          max_queue_ms: "25"              # allow a little more queueing rather than OOMing
          enable_backpressure: "true"

      kv_cache:
        page_size_kb: "64"
        reserved_vram_fraction: "0.22"
        compaction:
          enabled: "true"
          trigger_fragmentation_pct: "6.0"
          max_compaction_ms_per_minute: "250"

      memory:
        allocator: "cuda_malloc_async"
        fragmentation_oom_guard: "true"

      host_recommendations:
        required:
          - "nvidia_driver_min"
        best_effort:
          - "cpu_pinning"
          - "numa_alignment"
        notes: "L40S is OOM-sensitive; do not raise concurrency without rerunning benchmark matrix + burst tests."

      observability:
        emit_profile_tags: "true"
        log_startup_summary: "true"
        kernel_choice_metric: "true"
        scheduler_queue_ms_metric: "true"


  # L40S fallback
  - profile_id: "l40s-fallback-safe-v1"
    priority: 10
    status: "active"
    description: "Very conservative L40S fallback; use during instability / incident mitigation."

    selectors:
      gpu:
        sku: "L40S"
      workload:
        bucket: "any"

    guardrails:
      min_free_vram_gb: "8.0"
      max_gpu_util_p99_target: "0.80"
      max_concurrent_requests: "20"
      max_inflight_tokens: "24000"
      max_queue_depth: "45"

    knobs:
      kernel:
        attention:
          implementation: "auto"
          allow_fallback: "true"
          fallback_order: "flash,triton"
        matmul:
          fp8_enabled: "false"
          bf16_accumulation: "true"

      scheduler:
        mode: "continuous_batching"
        max_batch_tokens: "3072"
        max_batch_size: "16"
        prefill_decode_policy: "prefill_priority"
        queueing:
          max_queue_ms: "20"
          enable_backpressure: "true"

      kv_cache:
        page_size_kb: "64"
        reserved_vram_fraction: "0.24"
        compaction:
          enabled: "true"
          trigger_fragmentation_pct: "5.0"
          max_compaction_ms_per_minute: "200"

      memory:
        allocator: "cuda_malloc_async"
        fragmentation_oom_guard: "true"

      host_recommendations:
        required:
          - "nvidia_driver_min"
        best_effort:
          - "cpu_pinning"
        notes: "Rollback target for L40S OOM/fragmentation incidents."

      observability:
        emit_profile_tags: "true"
        log_startup_summary: "true"
        kernel_choice_metric: "true"
        scheduler_queue_ms_metric: "true"


Validation rules (draft, incomplete)
- profile_id must be unique.
- For any supported sku + deployment mode, there must exist at least one profile with selectors matching bucket:any (pack_fallback behavior).
- Guardrails must be internally consistent with knobs:
  - max_concurrent_requests <= scheduler-derived admission control limit
  - reserved_vram_fraction + min_free_vram_gb must leave non-negative available VRAM given vram_gb (if known)
  - max_inflight_tokens must be <= function(max_concurrent_requests, max_context_tokens_lte) (TBD formula)
- If software.driver/cuda constraints don’t match the host, runtime behavior depends on compatibility_mode:
  - strict: refuse to start and emit a clear error + remediation
  - permissive: start with fallback-safe profile + disable certain features (e.g., fp8)


Open questions / TODOs
1) Where do “workload buckets” come from?
   - Option A: inferred dynamically by runtime (prompt length + expected output length + concurrency) and used to pick profile.
   - Option B: pre-configured per route/model in control plane.
   - Concern: dynamic selection may cause “profile flapping” under mixed traffic.

2) Profile selection timing
   - Startup-only vs per-model-load vs per-request.
   - Current leaning: choose base profile at startup (sku/software/deployment), then apply per-model modifiers at model load (model family, quantization), and do NOT change per request.

3) How do we represent model family and quantization reliably?
   - Need normalized model metadata for open model zoo + customer models.
   - Quantization interactions (int8/fp8) might require separate profiles or separate capability flags.

4) MIG support
   - Do we support MIG at all for Hosted? Infra suggests mostly no-MIG, but Private customers might.
   - If MIG enabled, should we treat each MIG profile as a separate “SKU” in selectors?

5) Host recommendations enforcement
   - Should host_recommendations.required be enforced (fail fast) in Dedicated/Hosted?
   - Example: hugepages are not always safe; probably best-effort only.

6) Profile version pinning
   - Do we support pinning pack_version only, or also pinning profile_id?
   - Dedicated customer workflow likely wants: pin pack_version + optionally a stable profile_id.

7) Cardinality concerns for metrics
   - If we tag everything with profile_id, do we exceed metrics cardinality limits?
   - Maybe tag only with pack_version + sku by default; profile_id tag gated behind debug mode?

8) How do we do rollbacks?
   - Is rollback “switch pack_version” globally or per cohort?
   - Need an explicit kill switch semantics: disable profile pack entirely vs revert to fallback-safe profile.

9) JSON typing
   - Some fields above are shown as strings for simplicity, but compiled config should use real types.
   - Need to confirm runtime config loader supports numbers/bools consistently (ENG-4922).


Notes from recent discussions (Jan–Feb 2026)
- Kernel team prefers explicit attention implementation selection w/ fallback order (Hiro/Grace).
- Scheduler team wants explicit queue limits and backpressure toggles exposed as profile knobs (Sofia/Marcus).
- SRE/Infra pushing for strict compatibility gates on driver/CUDA mismatches to avoid weird silent regressions (Neha/Irene/Sean).

Next steps
- Convert this into a “schema + examples” PR behind a feature flag (see github:redwood/pr-24873).
- Add a minimal validator (unique ids, required fallback, numeric ranges).
- Decide the minimal stable knob set for v1 (cut anything not wired end-to-end).
